family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A counter starts at 0 and is bounded between 0 and cap (inclusive). events is a list of strings, each one of "inc" (increase the counter by 1, unless it is already at cap, in which case it stays), "dec" (decrease the counter by 1, unless it is already at 0, in which case it stays), or "reset" (set the counter back to 0). Return the final counter value after processing all events in order.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A bank account starts at balance 0. events is a list where each item is ("deposit", amt), ("withdraw", amt), or ("month_end",). A deposit adds amt to the balance. A withdrawal subtracts amt from the balance only if the balance is at least amt, otherwise it is skipped. A month_end event applies interest: the balance is multiplied by (1 + rate) and rounded to 2 decimal places. Return the final balance rounded to 2 decimal places.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: An elevator starts at floor min_floor with its door "CLOSED". commands is a list of strings: "open" sets the door to "OPEN", "close" sets the door to "CLOSED", and "up"/"down" move the elevator one floor up or down (bounded within [min_floor, max_floor]) but only take effect while the door is CLOSED; while the door is OPEN, "up" and "down" commands are ignored. Return a tuple (final_floor, final_door_state) after processing all commands in order.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A traffic light starts at RED and normally cycles RED -> GREEN -> YELLOW -> RED, advancing one step in this cycle for every "tick" event. events is a list of strings, each "tick" or "emergency". An "emergency" event immediately forces the light back to RED, and the next "tick" after an emergency advances to GREEN, exactly as if the cycle had just restarted. Return the final light state (one of "RED", "GREEN", "YELLOW") after processing all events in order.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: Simulate a shopping cart. events is a list where each item is ("add", item, qty, price) which adds qty units of item to the cart at the given unit price (updating the stored price and adding to any existing quantity of that item), ("remove", item, qty) which reduces the quantity of item by qty (removing the item entirely from the cart if the resulting quantity would be zero or less; removing an item not in the cart does nothing), or ("clear",) which empties the cart. Return the total cost of everything currently in the cart, computed as the sum over items of quantity times unit price.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A turnstile starts LOCKED. events is a list of strings, each "coin" or "push". A "coin" event sets the state to UNLOCKED. A "push" event, only when the state is UNLOCKED, locks the turnstile again and counts as one successful pass; a push while LOCKED has no effect. Return a tuple (final_state, pass_count) after processing all events in order.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A robot vacuum starts at (0, 0) facing north ("N") on a grid, and obstacles is a list of (x, y) coordinate tuples it cannot enter. commands is a list of single characters: "L" turns the robot 90 degrees counter-clockwise in place, "R" turns it 90 degrees clockwise in place, and "F" moves it one unit forward in its current facing direction unless the destination cell is in obstacles, in which case the robot stays where it is. Every cell the robot occupies (including its starting cell) counts as cleaned. Return the number of distinct cells cleaned after processing all commands.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A parking garage charges by time. events is a list of (op, car_id, time) tuples where op is "enter" or "exit" and time is a non-negative integer. An "enter" records the car's arrival time, unless that car is already parked, in which case it is ignored. An "exit" for a car that is currently parked computes a fee of (exit_time - enter_time) * rate and removes the car from the parked set; an "exit" for a car that is not currently parked is ignored. Return a dict mapping each car_id that successfully exited to its computed fee.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A traffic light for cars cycles forever: RED for red_duration ticks then GREEN for green_duration ticks, starting RED at tick 0. Pedestrians can only cross while the car light is RED. arrivals is a list of non-negative integers giving the tick at which each pedestrian arrives, in the order they arrive. Each pedestrian crosses at the first tick that is greater than or equal to their arrival time and during which the car light is RED. Return a list of the crossing ticks, one per pedestrian, in the same order as arrivals.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: Simulate a simple undo/redo document. commands is a list where each item is ("do", value) which appends value to the end of the document and clears any pending redo history, ("undo",) which removes the last value in the document (moving it to the redo history), doing nothing if the document is empty, or ("redo",) which re-appends the most recently undone value from the redo history, doing nothing if there is no such value. Return the final document as a list, in order, after processing all commands.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A voting gate starts CLOSED. events is a list of strings, each "yes" or "no", and threshold is a positive integer. Maintain a running net score that increases by 1 for each "yes" and decreases by 1 for each "no". As soon as the net score reaches threshold or higher, the gate becomes OPEN and stays OPEN permanently, ignoring all further events. Return the final gate state as the string "OPEN" or "CLOSED".

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A coffee machine has a dict prices mapping drink name to price and a dict stock mapping drink name to units remaining. events is a list of (op, value) tuples: ("insert", amount) adds amount to the current credit, and ("select", drink) dispenses one unit of drink, subtracting its price from the credit and its count from stock, but only if drink has stock remaining greater than 0 and the current credit is at least its price; otherwise the selection is ignored and nothing changes. Return a tuple (final_credit, final_stock, total_dispensed) where final_stock is the stock dict after all dispenses and total_dispensed counts successful selections. The input stock dict must not be modified.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A bank account starts at balance 0. events is a list of (op, amount) tuples where op is "deposit" or "withdraw". A deposit adds amount to the balance. A withdrawal removes amount plus a flat fee from the balance, but only if the balance is at least amount + fee; otherwise the withdrawal (and its fee) is skipped entirely and the balance is unchanged. Return the final balance after processing all events in order.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: An elevator starts at start_floor and sweeps one floor at a time in the given direction (1 for up, -1 for down), stopping only at floors that appear in requests (a list of ints), until it reaches floor 1 (if going down) or top_floor (if going up), at which point the sweep ends after checking that final floor too. Return a list of the floors stopped at, in the order they are visited.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: A robot starts at (0, 0) with a given amount of fuel. commands is a list of single characters, each "N", "S", "E", or "W", meaning move one unit in that direction. Each successful move consumes 1 unit of fuel; once fuel reaches 0, no further moves happen (remaining commands are ignored, though fuel never goes negative). Return a tuple ((x, y), remaining_fuel) giving the final position and remaining fuel after processing all commands in order.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: Simulate a retail checkout register. events is a list where each item is ("scan", price) which adds price to the current transaction, ("void",) which removes the most recently scanned item from the current transaction (doing nothing if the transaction is empty), or ("pay",) which finalizes the current transaction, recording its total (the sum of its remaining scanned prices), and starts a new empty transaction. Any items scanned after the last "pay" event with no following "pay" are not included in any total. Return a list of the finalized transaction totals, in the order the "pay" events occurred.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: There are n lights in a row, indexed 0 to n-1, all starting off. events is a list where each item is ("toggle", i) which flips light i between on and off, ("toggle_all",) which flips every light, or ("reset",) which turns every light off. Return the final list of n booleans (True for on, False for off) after processing all events in order.
hidden_tests: assert light_switch_group(5, [('toggle_all',), ('toggle_all',)]) == [False, False, False, False, False]
assert light_switch_group(5, [('toggle', 1), ('toggle', 3), ('toggle_all',)]) == [True, False, True, False, True]
assert light_switch_group(6, [('toggle', 0), ('toggle', 1), ('toggle', 2), ('toggle', 3), ('toggle', 4), ('toggle', 5)]) == [True, True, True, True, True, True]
assert light_switch_group(6, [('toggle', 0), ('toggle', 2), ('toggle', 4)]) == [True, False, True, False, True, False]
assert light_switch_group(5, [('toggle', 0), ('toggle', 4), ('toggle_all',), ('toggle', 2)]) == [False, True, False, True, False]

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: Simulate a waiting line with a server that can handle several people at once. events is a list where each item is ("arrive", person_id) which adds person_id to the back of the queue, or ("serve",) which removes up to capacity people from the front of the queue (fewer if the queue has fewer than capacity people waiting). Return the final queue contents as a list, ordered from front to back, after processing all events in order.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: Track a loan balance. events is a list of (op, amount) tuples where op is "borrow" or "repay" and amount is a non-negative number. A borrow increases the debt by amount without limit. A repay decreases the debt by amount, but the debt can never go below 0: if amount exceeds the current debt, the debt simply becomes 0 and the excess is not carried over or refunded. Return the final debt after processing all events in order.

family: simple simulations and state machines (bank balances over transactions, elevator stops, traffic lights)
spec: Two independent traffic lights each cycle forever through RED, then GREEN, then YELLOW, then back to RED, starting RED at tick 0; durations_a and durations_b are each a tuple (red_ticks, green_ticks, yellow_ticks) giving the two lights' own phase durations. Given n_ticks (a non-negative integer), count how many ticks t in range 0 to n_ticks - 1 (inclusive of 0, exclusive of n_ticks) have both lights showing GREEN at the same time. Return that count.
